meta_title: AI assistants and internal tools | AWA
meta_description: Website chat that answers from your content and hands over to a person, plus internal tools that draft invoices and quotes and take on repeat work.
hero_title: Answers from your content. | A person when it counts.
hero_lead: Website chat that answers from your pages and documents, shows its sources, and hands over when a person should decide. Plus small internal tools that take repetitive work off your team and leave a draft for review.
included_intro: Everything here is scoped to your content and your process. Your team reviews each draft before it is sent or saved, and the chat hands over when a person should decide.

included.title: Website chat on your content
included.text: An assistant that answers from your pages and documents, so replies reflect your business rather than generic AI answers.

included.title: Sources and human handover
included.text: Answers can show the page or document they came from. When a person should decide, the chat hands over.

included.title: Email, documents, invoices and quotes
included.text: Incoming email, documents, invoices and quotes are turned into drafts. Your team reviews each one before it is sent or saved.

included.title: Dashboards and admin tools
included.text: Small internal dashboards and admin tools for repeat jobs, so your team has one place to review the work.

included.title: Guardrails, logging and privacy
included.text: We set limits on what the assistant can say and do, log what it did, and include the privacy settings you ask for.

included.title: Your choice of model
included.text: OpenAI, Anthropic Claude or Google Gemini. We choose with you for the job, and we tell you which model is in use.

use_cases.situation: You get the same after-hours questions about service area, call-out timing, and whether the job needs a visit.
use_cases.what_we_do: We train a website assistant on your pages and documents. It shows its sources and hands over when a customer wants an exact quote.
use_cases.outcome: People get a straight answer after hours. You step in for the quote, with the question already clear.

use_cases.situation: Your team is with customers on the floor, while the same sizing, stock and shipping questions keep arriving on the site.
use_cases.what_we_do: We add a chat assistant grounded in your product pages and policies. It hands over returns and custom-order questions, and anything else it should not decide.
use_cases.outcome: Shoppers get answers from your own pages while you serve the floor. Your team takes the questions that need a human.

use_cases.situation: Invoices, quotes and supplier emails arrive all week, and someone retypes the same fields every afternoon.
use_cases.what_we_do: We build a tool that reads those emails and documents and fills in a draft invoice or quote. Your team reviews it before it goes out.
use_cases.outcome: The copying is done before anyone checks it. Your people spend their time on the figures, then approve or correct the draft.

faq.q: Who will I actually work with?
faq.a: You work with Chris Conen. He supervises Architect and Astra, the AI engineers who write, test and review the code. One point of contact, no account manager, Australia-wide. Chris built and runs NEXUS, our website chatbot, which answers from the studio's own content. He also uses an AI-assisted pipeline that audited and rewrote 152 website templates, each checked visually.

faq.q: What does the assistant answer, and when does it hand over?
faq.a: It answers from your pages and documents, and it can show the source. Where that material is silent, or you want a person to decide, it hands over. The plumbing demo on this page does that for an exact quote. We set those rules with you.

faq.q: Does the Privacy Act cover a small business?
faq.a: The OAIC says the Privacy Act 1988 covers organisations with annual turnover of more than $3 million and Australian Government agencies. Most small businesses with annual turnover of $3 million or less are not covered, except listed cases: health service providers, trading in personal information, Commonwealth contracts and residential tenancy databases. We work to that guidance. Ask a lawyer.

faq.q: What privacy-policy change starts on 10 December 2026?
faq.a: The OAIC said on 30 September 2026 that from 10 December 2026, APP 1.8 will require an APP entity's privacy policy to state the kinds of personal information a program uses to make, or substantially help make, a decision that could significantly affect a person's rights or interests, and the decisions involved. We work to APP 1.8; ask a lawyer.

faq.q: If a chatbot misleads a customer, are we liable?
faq.a: The ACCC's submission to the Parliamentary Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence says a business would be liable under the Australian Consumer Law for a misleading representation by an AI customer-service chatbot, just as for its website or an employee. We keep answers tied to your sources and hand over rather than guess. Ask a lawyer about your own obligations.

cta_title: Show us the work you repeat
cta_text: You deal with Chris Conen as your one point of contact, and we work Australia-wide. Bring the questions customers ask and the documents your team retypes. We will say what an assistant can answer, what it should hand over, and what should stay a draft for review.
